title: Impact of Private Hire Vehicles on Taxi Drivers' Income
what_it_is: Impact of Private Hire Vehicles on Taxi Drivers' Income

sections.label: Taxi income and mileage standards
sections.summary: Average monthly net income rose about 5% in real terms, and most taxis meet daily minimum mileage standards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Average monthly net income has, however, increased by about 5% in real terms due to lower fuel costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Today, about 80% of all taxis are able to meet the daily minimum mileage requirement of 250 kilometres per day.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Of these taxis, more than three quarters ply more than 300 kilometres per day.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In addition, the proportion of two-shift taxis has increased from 53% to 68% since the introduction of the standards.

sections.label: Reviewing taxi availability standards
sections.summary: The government is monitoring the situation and will review taxi availability standards at the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For example, during weekends, the standard is that 75% of a taxi company's fleet must meet the daily minimum mileage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: With the growth of hailing apps and the private hire car industry in recent years, there may be room for us to adjust the taxi availability standards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: As I had updated Parliament earlier, we are monitoring the situation closely and will review the standards at the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We are monitoring the situation closely, gathering data on commuters' preferences and the availability of taxis on the roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: So, where appropriate, we will further level the playing field for the industry and we will, as I said earlier, review the taxi availability framework with a balanced view towards commuters' needs and also the welfare of taxi drivers.
